subject: Private GPU pool sizing: capacity ask + procurement timeline
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@aurora-ai.com>, procurement@aurora-ai.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private GPU pool sizing: capacity ask + procurement timeline

Lina / Aurora procurement team — thanks again for the kickoff earlier today. Attached is a first-pass sizing worksheet and SOW draft so your architects and procurement can align on commitments. Summary of our ask and proposed cadence: 

- Throughput targets: steady-state 2.5M tokens/min (inference) with sustained 200 qps for 1k token average requests; 1.8x burst headroom to 360 qps for short windows (5–10m).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 350ms for standard gen requests (1k tokens); can tier to higher-latency, lower-cost nodes for non-critical batch workloads.
- Network egress: estimate 1.2 TB/day per 8-GPU slab at sustained qps (includes replication & logging).
- Warm-up: recommend pre-warmed KV caches and sticky routing for first 15–20m after cutover.

Next steps we propose:
1) Aurora to confirm peak/baseline qps window samples (we included the sample spreadsheet in the Drive link).
2) Redwood to finalize a rightsizing proposal and a quote for Dedicated private pool (includes support and 24/7 pager option).
3) Procurement: target mutual SOW review by EOD Fri 12/05 so legal can start redlines.

I've attached the rightsizing PDF with our conservative and aggressive scenarios — please share with your infra team. Happy to hop on a deep-dive tomorrow if useful.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@aurora-ai.com>

Cc: procurement@aurora-ai.com
Date: Thu, 04 Dec 2025 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool sizing: capacity ask + procurement timeline

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the files. A few clarifying questions from our infra and procurement leads before we push for SOW review: 

- Is the 1.8x burst modeled as additional reserved GPUs (slab overprovision) or as ephemeral burst that Redwood can absorb within tenant headroom? We need lane guarantees for our SLA.
- Can you confirm expected cold-start time when routing to a different slab (e.g., for canary/fallback)? Our ops team is sensitive to any 90s+ coldstart windows.
- The egress calc looks plausible but we need a sample per-request breakdown to run through our cost model — can you share a token-to-bytes mapping you used?

Procurement notes: we will need an outline of termination & data retention for the private control plane. Please include standard audit log retention options and KMS/HSM integration notes in the SOW.

Also copied Sanjay from CloudInfra — he's evaluating network peering options and wants to coordinate capacity planning for cross-connects.

Best,
Lina
VP Infrastructure, Aurora AI

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool sizing: capacity ask + procurement timeline

Quick technical clarifications from our side (Jonas here, runtime lead):

- Burst model: we recommend a hybrid approach. For guaranteed lane SLAs (Aurora's tier), we allocate reserved slabs sized to cover the 1.0x steady-state + 0.5x committed run-rate. The additional 1.8x peak is served by warm, pre-allocated burst slabs that are preemptible across lower-priority tenants and elastic within the private pool. That lets us hit latency SLOs while keeping costs reasonable.
- Cold-starts: with KV cache warmup and container prefetch, cross-slab cold-start to first token is typically 40–60s. Fully warmed latency profile resumes in ~2–3 minutes depending on model size and tokenizer. We can provide a canary routing policy to keep canary lanes hot for critical paths.
- Token-to-bytes mapping: average request 1k tokens -> ~28–34KB of payload (includes prompt + metadata + response envelope). The rightsizing doc used 32KB/request. We'll drop a per-request CSV in Drive for your cost model.

Operational notes: pre-warmed slabs require a small warm-pool (5–10% of committed capacity) for predictable burst absorption. Also recommend admission control: queueing window with graceful degradation to batch workers for non-SLO traffic.

I'll attach a short-run calculation in the Drive link and can run a quick simulation if Aurora shares representative traces.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Runtime Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 07 Dec 2025 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool sizing: capacity ask + procurement timeline

Lina / team — thanks for the quick feedback. Based on Jonas' notes I've updated the SOW draft (attached) to call out:

- Reservation tiers: Gold (dedicated slabs with guaranteed lane), Silver (committed capacity with burst access), Bronze (best-effort using elastic pool)
- Warm-pool sizing heuristic: 8% of committed capacity as a baseline (explicit formula in the SOW).
- Cold-start SLAs: 60s to first token for cross-slab warmup; 3m recovery for full KV and model caches. We will include a canary routing clause to maintain a minimal hot lane at all times for Gold customers.
- Networking & peering: proposed cross-connects and a 10Gbps egress profile per 8-GPU slab; Sanjay—please confirm whether that aligns with CloudInfra's recommended port sizing.
- Data retention & KMS: options included (30/90/365 days), and an HSM integration addendum for regulated data.

Action items and timeline: 
- Aurora infra to share 72h trace samples (CSV) by EOD Tue 12/09 so we can run a 7-day simulation.
- Redwood to provide final quote and SOW redline by Thu 12/11.
- Procurement to share preferred contract templates and payment cadence.

If everyone is OK, I'll schedule a 45m call Tues to walk the simulation inputs and procurement checkpoints.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
